result:
Both integrate one branch's changes into another. Difference is history shape.

**`git merge`**: joins two histories with a new merge commit (two parents). Existing commits unchanged. History shows the branch as it happened. Non-destructive.

**`git rebase`**: replays your commits on top of the target branch. Creates new commits with new hashes. History becomes linear, no merge commit. Rewrites history.

```
Before:        A---B---C  main
                    \
                     D---E  feature

merge:         A---B---C---M  main
                    \     /
                     D---E

rebase:        A---B---C---D'---E'  feature
```

Conflicts: merge resolves once, in the merge commit. Rebase can stop at each replayed commit.

Never rebase commits already pushed and shared. Hashes change, so teammates' history diverges from yours and a force push is needed.

Use rebase to tidy a local or private branch before sharing. Use merge to integrate shared branches.
